title: Burst replay tokens/sec investigator and CI harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a focused tokens-per-second microbenchmark and replay harness that simulates production-like microbursts and steady-state traffic for core models. This ticket covers: (1) a deterministic replay runner that consumes recorded request traces (short prompts, chat turns, embeddings) and emits controlled bursts and ramps; (2) integrated p95 and token-rate telemetry ingestion that tags runs with runtime flags (KV cache on/off, quantization profile, batch window); (3) CI jobs and a daily job that runs smoke and regression checks against core model variants; (4) automated regression detection with configurable thresholds and a PR blocking policy when throughput or p95 regress beyond guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: A replay harness that can ingest recorded request traces and replay them with configurable burst profiles (burst size, inter-burst gap, ramp rate).
Runs collect tokens/sec histograms and p95 latency per model variant and emit metrics to the performance metrics namespace with stable tag keys (model, config, seq_len_bucket, cache_enabled).
A CI job (ci/throughput/burst-replay) executes a small nightly suite and fails when tokens/sec drops >15% or p95 increases >20% compared to baseline for a model-config pair.
Dashboards created: Burst Replay overview, Model-config p95 trending, Regression alert feed — links added to ticket.
Playbook entry and runbook for investigating regressions (how to reproduce locally, key traces to inspect, recommended next steps) committed to the runbooks repo.
tasks: Design replay format (JSON lines): request_id, prompt_hash, seq_len, model, metadata, timestamp; ensure privacy-safe (strip PII).
Implement replay engine in Go with two modes: microburst and sustained; support concurrency and token pacing controls.
Instrument runner to export Prometheus metrics and structured logs with tokens_emitted_total, tokens_per_second_gauge, p95_latency_ms (labels: model, quant, cache, run_id).
Create CI pipeline: lightweight smoke (small sample), canary (larger sample), nightly full run; add gating thresholds and notification hooks to slack/perf-alerts.
Add baseline collection job to capture golden reference for core model variants and store artifact in s3://redwood-perf/goldens/runtime-1.21/
Build dashboard panels and alert rules; add to console-performance team dashboards and link in PR templates.
Write runbook: reproducible steps, how to run replay locally, how to interpret metric signatures for KV cache vs kernel path regressions.
risks: Recorded traces may contain sensitive content — must sanitize and validate before ingesting into CI artifacts.
False positives from noisy baselines if upstream infra variability is not controlled; need multiple runs and statistical smoothing.
CI job runtime and cost — full runs can be expensive; need to tier tests and keep full runs to nightly/weekly only.
Cross-model comparability: quantization and kernel differences mean absolute tokens/sec values vary; comparisons must be model-config scoped.
